text:
Maya Clarke: Quick random q — if you could teleport to any restaurant in the world right now, where would you go and what would you order? 30s answers :earth_americas:
Omar Singh: Noma in Copenhagen. The full tasting menu — salty, savory, weirdly delightful courses. :drooling_face:
Jin Park: IKEA in Älmhult for the meatballs and lingonberry juice. Cheap nostalgia, zero pretense. :meat_on_bone:
Priya Nair: Tiny izakaya in Shinjuku. Lots of yakitori, karaage, and a cold beer. Small tables, loud laughs. :beers:
Carlos Mendez: Taquería in CDMX. Al pastor, pineapple, lime, and a jug of horchata. Street-sauce levels please. :taco::tropical_drink:
Maya Clarke: Also tempted by a seaside spot in Lisbon that does salt-baked fish and grilled prawns. Ocean + garlic = instant happiness. :fish::ocean:
Jin Park: If teleportation includes ambience: a Studio Ghibli-esque outdoor bakery with warm milk bread and green tea. Pure comfort. :bread::herb:
Priya Nair: Low-key vote for a Parisian bistro too — onion soup + tiny espresso. Classic, instantly fancy. :croissant::coffee:
Omar Singh: We should do a hypothetical team rota — someone picks a place each month. Highly achievable in Slack dreamland. :calendar:
emoji-bot: Heads-up: teleportation is not covered by office travel policy. Reactions only. :robot_face:
Carlos Mendez: Adding a wildcard — midnight ramen spot in Fukuoka, slurp till you drop. Highly recommended. :ramen:
Maya Clarke: Lots of good recs. Saving this thread for future food envy. :bookmark_tabs:
